abstract: From business perspective of the internet of things, actualization of the IOT into the complex system will link the real world with the digital world seamlessly. Modeling the complex systems can be hard in a computational sense and much management of relationships exists. Two of the problems of IOT-based system are the lack of stable architecture and autonomous process. This paper proposes the intelligent service-integrated platform based on IOT technology using FCM and fuzzy QFD method. It aimed at simulating complex system linked physical and digital objects with casual relationships while quantifying the performance impact of decision-making efficiency.

articleTitle: Next generation sensor systems
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: As technology advances, and component and system costs drop, fiber optic and other sensor system applications are expected to proliferate, expanding from niche uses focused on high-value assets to increasing employment in consumer products and everyday life.

articleTitle: Nanostructured plasmonic devices and their applications
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this talk, we will review our recent works on nanostructured plasmonic devices, and their applications in high performance light absorption, photothermal effects, and partly in photonic integrations.

articleTitle: The design of an achromatic two dimensional deflection prism
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: An achromatic two dimensional deflection prism was designed for applications of autostereoscopic or multi-view projection display systems. The relation between the beam deflection and the wedges was analyzed theoretically. The dispersion free condition and the determination of the biprism wedge were discussed in detail.

articleTitle: High-speed semiconductor all-optical conversion device based on field-driven quantum well
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this paper, an InGaAsP/InGaAlAs high-band-offset quantum well for high-speed all-optical wavelength conversion is reviewed. Due to large band offset ratio between electron and heavy hole, InGaAsP/InGaAlAs multiple quantum well can have short carrier sweeping time under electric field from low hole band offset. Large than 33GHz of all-optical frequency response is demonstrated under high bias, confirming such material can be used for high speed all optical network.

articleTitle: 2.7µm emission properties of Er3+/Nd3+-codoped fluorotellurite glasses
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> singly doped and Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>/Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-codoped fluorotellurite glasses are prepared by melt-quenching method. The 2.7 μm emission spectra of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions in fluorotellurite glasses are investigated under 808nm excitation. The enhancement of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> 2.7 μm emission shows that Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> can be an effective sensitizer for Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> : <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11/2</sub>→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13/2</sub> transition, and the energy transfer efficiency can be as large as 84%. The absorption and emission cross sections are calculated using Füchtbauer-Ladenburg equation and McCumber theory with large values of 1.62×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-20</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 1.11×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-20</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The results suggest that the present glasses have potential applications in 2.7 μm laser materials.

articleTitle: Optical fibers for biomedical photonics applications
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Recent advances in photonics technology have generated extensive interests its application to basic life sciences research, to healthcare instruments, and to biomedical diagnosis, therapy, and imaging. Optical fibers play a key role in these applications owing to their unique physical and light-transmission properties. These properties enable fibers to resolve challenging issues such as collecting and transmitting low-level fluorescent light signals, delivering a wide range of optical power over a broad spectrum to a specific tissue area, and carrying out minimally invasive medical procedures. This talk addresses various fiber structures, materials, and spectral responses, and describes some biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Distributed birefringence measurement for optical fibers and fiber based devices
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper presents three different methods to measure distributed birefringence based on Brillouin grating, BOTDA and Brillouin beat OTDR. The spatial resolution of less than 1 m is demonstrated with birefringence range of centimeters to a few tens of meters.

articleTitle: Embedded fiber-optic sensors in carbon fiber composites for temperature-insensitive and intensity-modulated microdisplacement measurement
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The fiber-optic sensors generally need to be packaged for practical applications. Carbon fiber composite is an excellent package material due to its light weight, high toughness, ultrahigh Young's modulus (with tensile modulus of 420 GPa or more), good environmental resistance, etc., and it has been widely used for the aerospace and automotive fields. Here, we demonstrate our recent research achievements of embedding the FBG and photonic crystal fiber sensors in the carbon fiber composites for temperature-insensitive and intensity-modulated microdisplacement measurement.

articleTitle: A location aided cooperative caching protocol for mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2013 6th IEEE/International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Cooperative caching is an attractive solution for reducing bandwidth demands and network latency in mobile ad hoc networks. Deploying caches in mobile nodes can reduce the overall traffic considerably. Cache hits eliminate the need to contact the data source frequently, which avoids additional network overhead. In this paper we propose a data discovery and cache management policy for cooperative caching, which reduces the caching overhead and delay by reducing the number of control messages flooded in to the network. A cache discovery process based on location of neighboring nodes is developed for this. The cache replacement policy we propose aims at increasing the cache hit ratio. The simulation results gives a promising result based on the metrics of studies.
